# Test vectors for PBKDF2-HMAC, one per line:
#
#     set hash iterations password salt derived-key
#
# The password, the salt and the key are hex ("-" is empty). The hash is one of
# md5, sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha512-224 and sha512-256.
#
# "wycheproof" lines are Project Wycheproof's PBKDF2 vectors for SHA-1, SHA-224,
# SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 (testvectors_v1/pbkdf2_hmac*_test.json): all those
# that take fewer than 4096 iterations, and one in five of those that take 4096
# (all of them would make the test take seconds in a debug build). Not the two
# that take 80,000 and 16,777,216 iterations, which RFC 7914 and RFC 6070 have.
#
# "cross" lines cover all eight hashes at the lengths where an implementation
# can go wrong: a password of one block and one byte more (where HMAC starts
# hashing its key), salts on both sides of the point where the first message
# spills into a second block, output lengths around multiples of the hash's
# output, and 1 to 1000 iterations. Python's hashlib made them; Go's
# crypto/pbkdf2 and OpenSSL 3.6 (`openssl kdf PBKDF2`) agree on every one.
#
# Written by scripts kept outside the repository. Do not edit by hand.
